citation: Konrad Bach, Jonathan Ford, Robert Foley, Jacob Januszewski, Ryan Murtagh, Summer Decker, Juan S. Uribe. Morphometric Analysis of Lumbar Intervertebral Disc Height: An Imaging Study. World Neurosurg. (2019) 124:e106-e118 (April 2019; no issue number printed). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wneu.2018.12.014. Received 11 July 2018, accepted 3 December 2018. Conflict of interest: Uribe is a paid consultant for NuVasive (p. e118, PDF 13). Source: thread "Reread every paper for clinical detail", project symphony_4, 2026-10-28. Copy read: greg's upload of 2026-10-28 01:02 UTC (upload id 44635a7e-db3b-4a7a-936e-5dc02bbc1153); sha256 begins ef46b33cb9428dc7. PDF 1-13 = pp. e106-e118.
population: 240 anonymized abdominal CT scans of living patients, 131 women and 109 men, University of South Florida (Tampa, Florida, USA), January 2010 to August 2012, collected prospectively after IRB approval; people aged 10-80 with a non-spinal complaint in whom thoracic and lumbar CT was obtained; anyone with incidental spinal pathology excluded (number excluded not given); ethnicity not reported (p. e107, PDF 2). Decade groups women/men: 10s 8/8, 20s 25/19, 30s 18/17, 40s 23/8, 50s 25/23, 60s 17/22, 70s 15/12 (Table 1, p. e108, PDF 3). Ages printed inconsistently: abstract 45 (14-83) women, 48 (14-89) men; results 45 (14-79) and 47 (14-79); methods 10-80. Table 6 N = 109 men, 131 women at every level. Stature, weight, BMI only for 81 women (46.5 +/- 17.8 y, 163.8 +/- 6.93 cm, 76.2 +/- 17.5 kg, BMI 28.4 +/- 6.13) and 69 men (48.5 +/- 19.3 y, 179.1 +/- 6.71 cm, 90 +/- 20.2 kg, BMI 27.9 +/- 5.4) (Tables 9-11, p. e115-e117, PDF 10-12); Inference: stature mostly whole inches, probably not measured.
modality: CT (scanner, slice thickness, kernel, voxel size not reported) modelled in Mimics Innovation Suite 19.0 (Materialise); bone threshold 226-3071 HU; each vertebra cut free by hand of the adjacent articular processes and, for T12, the 12th rib; points placed on the 3D bone surface in the midsagittal plane (disc heights) and on the pedicle borders (foraminal height) (p. e107, PDF 2; Figure 1). One neuroradiologist, blinded to age and sex, measured every scan once. Statistics: independent t-tests by sex, paired t-test left vs right FH (result not given), Pearson R with age graded weak 0.1-0.39, moderate 0.4-0.59, strong > 0.6; SPSS 24.0, P < 0.05 (pp. e107-e108, PDF 2-3; Tables 7-8).
levels_covered: Six discs T12/L1, L1/2, L2/3, L3/4, L4/5, L5/S1, with left and right foraminal heights at each (Tables 2-8). Level identification and counting not stated; Figure 1C shows six bodies above the sacrum (Inference: T12-L5 over S1). No cervical or thoracic discs; C2/C3 and C7/T1 not studied.

anomalies.variant: LSTV, sacralisation, lumbarisation, L6, T13, rib-count variants, block vertebrae
anomalies.finding: Not mentioned: no prevalence, no handling rule, no statement of how levels were counted; whether transitional spines were excluded as spinal pathology or measured under a 12-thoracic, 5-lumbar count cannot be told.
The 12th rib was cut away from T12 during segmentation, so T12 carried the 12th rib (Inference: 12-rib count); Figure 1C shows six bodies above the sacrum (Inference: T12-L5).
anomalies.how_identified: 3D CT model; rib separated by hand

anomalies.variant: Possible hidden transitional discs in the L5/S1 row (Inference)
anomalies.finding: Inference, prevalence from memory not from this paper: with roughly 10-20 percent LSTV in most series, the L5/S1 row may mix in L5/L6 discs or discs above a sacralised L5; the L5/S1 anterior height has the widest SD in Table 6 (2.59 men, 2.94 women), which such mixing or lordosis variation would produce.

measures.name: Anterior disc height
measures.definition: Midsagittal distance between the anterior edge of the inferior endplate of the cranial body and the anterior edge of the superior endplate of the caudal body; paper: "anterior edge, center, and posterior edge of each vertebra"; endplate assignment read from Figure 1A. Straight vs perpendicular distance not stated.
measures.projection: CT 3D bone surface model (Mimics), midsagittal plane, points placed by hand
measures.page: p. e107 (PDF 2), Figure 1; Table 6, p. e113 (PDF 8); Tables 2-3, p. e110-e111 (PDF 5-6)
measures.level_pattern: Men vs women (mm, Table 6): T12/L1 6.29+/-1.49 vs 4.81+/-1.09; L1/2 7.59+/-1.58 vs 5.92+/-1.27; L2/3 8.70+/-1.67 vs 7.13+/-1.51; L3/4 9.66+/-1.75 vs 8.11+/-1.62; L4/5 10.94+/-2.15 vs 9.82+/-2.28; L5/S1 11.92+/-2.59 vs 11.36+/-2.94. Rises monotonically to L5/S1, the only directly measured height still rising there. Inference: adjacent steps 1.0-1.7 mm, 0.4-0.9 pooled SD; orders levels on average only.
measures.covariates: Sex P 0.000 at every level except L5/S1 (0.123); men/women ratio 1.31 at T12/L1 falling to 1.05 at L5/S1 (Inference). Age, men: only L4/5 R -0.202 (P 0.035). Age, women (Table 8 first column, mislabelled Average): L3/4 -0.265, L4/5 -0.387, L5/S1 -0.388. Women's L4/5 11.33 (30s) to 9.06 (40s), L5/S1 13.8 to 10.32 (Table 3). Not tested against stature.
measures.error: Not reported; one observer, one pass. Between-subject SD 1.1-2.9 mm, CV about 18-26 percent (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: body subregion of the two consecutive instances (or instance cut anterior to the pedicles); vertebra's own midsagittal (symmetry) plane; anteriormost point of the caudal surface of the cranial body and of the cranial surface of the caudal body; straight distance, and the cranio-caudal component along the mean body axis as a second value; exclude marginal osteophytes.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, anterior rim to anterior rim; correct magnification or use a ratio; not on AP. Paper only says radiograph disc heights need complex corrections (p. e106, PDF 1).

measures.name: Middle disc height (centre)
measures.definition: Midsagittal distance between the centres of the facing endplates (centre point midway between anterior and posterior rim points in Figure 1B).
measures.projection: CT 3D bone surface model, midsagittal plane
measures.page: p. e107 (PDF 2), Figure 1A-B; Table 6, p. e113 (PDF 8)
measures.level_pattern: Men vs women (Table 6): T12/L1 6.66+/-1.34 vs 6.13+/-1.04; L1/2 8.20+/-1.82 vs 7.18+/-1.22; L2/3 9.79+/-1.87 vs 8.51+/-1.46; L3/4 10.41+/-1.86 vs 9.16+/-1.54; L4/5 10.64+/-1.76 vs 9.70+/-1.79; L5/S1 9.34+/-2.12 vs 9.13+/-2.00. Peaks at L4/5, falls at L5/S1; exceeds anterior from T12/L1 to L3/4, about equal at L4/5, about 0.8 x anterior at L5/S1 (Inference). L2/3-L4/5 steps 0.1-0.45 SD: does not separate them.
measures.covariates: Sex P 0.001 at T12/L1, 0.000 L1/2-L4/5, 0.444 L5/S1; men 9-15 percent larger above L5/S1 (Inference). Age, men: T12/L1 R 0.403, L1/2 0.341, L2/3 0.258 (rise), none below; men's T12/L1 5.63 (10s) to 7.48 (70s). Women: only L1/2 R 0.195.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: on the midsagittal plane, gap between the two bodies at the AP midpoint of the endplates, on the outer bone surface (226 HU boundary), so it includes both endplate concavities; a minimum gap or fitted-plane gap reads lower.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: a lateral radiograph projects the rims, not the midsagittal dome, so a radiographic mid-disc height underestimates this CT value; not on AP.

measures.name: Posterior disc height
measures.definition: Midsagittal distance between the posterior edges of the facing endplates (endplate assignment from Figure 1A).
measures.projection: CT 3D bone surface model, midsagittal plane
measures.error: Not reported. CV about 20-27 percent, the largest relative spread (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: posteriormost points of the two facing body surfaces on the midsagittal plane at the canal side; pedicle must not remain in the body mask; exclude posterior osteophytes.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, posterior rim to posterior rim; not on AP.

measures.name: Average disc height (three-point mean)
measures.definition: Mean of anterior, middle and posterior heights (p. e107). Table 6's row labelled Average is NOT this (it equals (anterior+posterior)/2; Inference from arithmetic); the decade tables label it correctly.
measures.projection: Derived from the CT midsagittal points
measures.page: Abstract p. e106 (PDF 1); p. e108 (PDF 3); Figure 8 p. e113 (PDF 8); Tables 2-3
measures.covariates: Women smaller except at L5/S1 (text, P < 0.001). Age, men: T12/L1 +0.265, L1/2 +0.211; women: L3/4 -0.304, L4/5 -0.291, L5/S1 -0.252. Teenagers smaller than 20s at every level (Tables 2-3).
measures.error: Not reported. Abstract SDs lie within 0.1 mm of Table 6's AP-average SDs (Inference); no table gives the SD of the three-point mean.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: mean of the three mask heights; inherits the middle height's concavity dependence.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: not reproducible from a lateral radiograph because the middle point differs (see middle height).

measures.name: Anterior-posterior average disc height (AP Avg)
measures.definition: Mean of anterior and posterior heights only (p. e107; footnote of Tables 2-3); Table 6's row labelled Average disc height.
measures.projection: Derived from the CT midsagittal rim points
measures.page: p. e107 (PDF 2); Table 6, p. e113 (PDF 8); Tables 2-3
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: mean of the anterior and posterior mask heights.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: the disc measure closest to what a lateral radiograph gives (rims only).

measures.name: Disc wedge, anterior minus posterior and anterior/posterior ratio (derived, Inference)
measures.definition: Not reported by the paper; computed from Table 6 means (ratio of means, no SD).
measures.projection: Derived; ratio is magnification-free on a lateral radiograph
measures.covariates: Women less wedged than men above L5/S1, nearly equal at it (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: from the same anterior and posterior points; a disc angle would need endplate depth, not given.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph or fluoroscopy, ratio of anterior to posterior rim heights.

measures.name: Foraminal height (FH), left and right
measures.definition: Greatest distance between the inferior border of the cranial pedicle and the superior border of the caudal pedicle on each side; paper: distances "furthest apart along the superior and inferior pedicle borders"; Table 6 reports the left-right average. Vertical span vs longest chord not stated.
measures.projection: CT 3D bone model; plane not stated (Inference: parasagittal through the pedicles)
measures.page: p. e107 (PDF 2), Figure 1A-B; Tables 4-6, p. e112-e113 (PDF 7-8)
measures.levels: T12/L1 to L5/S1, left and right
measures.covariates: Sex P 0.000, 0.000, 0.001, 0.025, 0.387, 0.806. Age, men: L2/3 -0.247, L3/4 -0.355, L4/5 -0.430, L5/S1 -0.415; women every level -0.241 to -0.447. Men's L4/5 18.77 (10s) to 16.39 (70s); women's L3/4 18.89 to 15.49. Left-right within 1 mm in 81 of 84 decade cells; left > right at men's L4/5, right > left at women's T12/L1 and L5/S1 in all decades (Inference).
measures.error: Not reported; paired left-right test result not given. CV 8-14 percent (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: needs pedicles of both instances (S1 pedicle from the sacrum mask at L5/S1); lowest point of the cranial pedicle's inferior border to highest point of the caudal pedicle's superior border, maximum cranio-caudal distance in the parasagittal plane through the pedicles; average sides.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph pedicle to pedicle, the two sides superimposed (roughly the average); correct magnification or use a ratio; not on AP.

level_details.detail: Smallest of the six discs in every disc height (anterior 6.29/4.81, middle 6.66/6.13, posterior 3.75/3.29, AP avg 5.02/4.05 mm, men/women); FH 16.27/15.35 second smallest after L5/S1; largest sex ratio at the anterior rim (1.31, Inference); men's middle height rises with age R 0.403 (the strongest positive age effect); in women no disc height changes with age but FH does (R -0.275); 12th rib cut from T12.
level_details.page: Table 6, p. e113 (PDF 8); Tables 7-8, p. e114 (PDF 9); p. e107, e109 (PDF 2, 4)

level_details.detail: Second smallest in every disc height; men's middle (R 0.341) and three-point average (0.211) rise with age; women's middle rises (0.195), posterior falls (-0.186).
FH peaks (19.46/18.63 mm); men's middle rises with age (0.258); women's posterior (-0.315) and AP average (-0.221) fall.

No disc height changes with age in men, FH falls (-0.355); in women posterior height falls most of any disc height (R -0.424) and FH most of all (-0.447); posterior height no longer differs by sex (P 0.079).

Highest middle and posterior heights; men's highest three-point average (9.2 mm), named by the authors the maximum interbody height (conclusion values 8.9/8.6 do not match their own results); anterior now exceeds middle; FH no sex difference (P 0.387), strongest men's FH decline (R -0.430); only level where men's anterior, posterior and AP average fall with age.

Largest anterior height (11.92/11.36), middle 9.34/9.13, posterior 5.27/5.23, most wedged (Inference); no sex difference in any measure (P 0.123-0.851), authors say about the same height; in men only FH changes with age (-0.415); FH smallest of all (14.30/14.36); widest anterior SD (2.59/2.94); women's anterior 13.8 mm in the 30s, 9.35 +/- 3.5 in the 70s; excluded from the elliptization pattern.

errors.value: None reported: one neuroradiologist, single pass, no intra- or inter-observer study, no phantom
Slice thickness, voxel size, scanner not given; bone surface at 226-3071 HU threshold with manual separation; Inference: z spacing limits disc-height precision
Recumbent CT may differ from standing; MRI may give different heights; trends expected to hold
14 sex-decade groups may be too small to show trends; statistical and clinical significance need not coincide; stature data only 81 women, 69 men
0.8-2.9 mm disc heights, 1.5-2.1 mm FH (population spread, not error)
Nine of 252 derived decade cells disagree with their components by 0.09-0.63 mm (Inference from arithmetic)

pearls_pitfalls.text: Indication: interbody cage height for lumbar fusion; restore disc height and FH (indirect decompression) without oversizing; cited complication papers mostly lateral interbody fusion, the cage-height study TLIF (ref 20).
pearls_pitfalls.page: p. e106 (PDF 1); p. e110 (PDF 5); refs p. e117-e118

pearls_pitfalls.text: Authors conclude a cage over 10 mm restores the interbody space beyond physiological height and may predispose to complications; measured heights were below typical cage sizes.
Recommended: cages 6-10 mm chosen by sex and overall body height, mid-body placement, maximum width, lordotic rather than square profile.

Reported cage heights 11.25 +/- 1.32 to 12.38 +/- 1.43 mm (ref 20) against the largest average disc height 9.87 +/- 0.7 mm (men, eighth decade, a group no table shows); oversizing raises implant-endplate pressure and may cost lordosis. Inference: anterior heights at L5/S1 reach 11.4-11.9 mm on average and 13.2-13.8 mm in women in their 20s-30s.
Subsidence is the main complication of excess endplate pressure; no unified grading system; cage height, anterior vs posterior placement, width and lordosis contribute; a prospective study is needed.

Elliptization: upper lumbar middle height rises with age while rims are unchanged; lower lumbar (not L5/S1) rims fall while middle is unchanged; authors admit it is not unequivocally shown and their tables support it only in part.
pearls_pitfalls.page: p. e110 (PDF 5); p. e116 (PDF 11); Figure 9 p. e117

pearls_pitfalls.text: FH falls with age more strongly and more often than disc height; authors attribute it to vertebral remodelling (endplate concavity, loss of body height), stiffer nucleus and loss of bone mass.
Pitfall: ageing and degeneration are separate processes; the belief that healthy discs narrow with age is not supported.
Sex matters more than age; cause unclear (BMI or muscle mass); effect of stature and weight left open.
Literature pitfalls: radiograph disc heights need complex corrections; MRI rests on a 2D sagittal section and is not broken down by level and decade; CT data scarce.

instructions.text: Measure each lumbar disc at three midsagittal points (anterior rim, endplate centre, posterior rim) between the facing endplates and keep all three.
Compare overall height with the abstract/Figure 8 three-point means; treat Table 6's Average row as the AP average (Inference from arithmetic).
On lateral radiographs or fluoroscopy measure only rim heights and pedicle-to-pedicle FH; do not equate a radiographic mid-disc height with the CT centre height (Inference).
Use ratios on radiographs: anterior/posterior about 1.4-1.8 at T12/L1-L4/5, about 2.2 at L5/S1; ratios of means, centres only (Inference).

Lumbosacral junction: greatest anterior height and wedge, middle about 20 percent below anterior, FH about 3 mm (17-19 percent) below the disc above (Inference from Table 6); confirm by sacral shape, never by disc numbers alone (Inference).

Thoracolumbar junction: expect T12/L1 to be the smallest of the six measured discs (posterior 3.3-3.8, anterior 4.8-6.3 mm); separate the 12th rib from T12; the paper has no disc above T12/L1, so confirm the junction by the last rib-bearing vertebra (Inference).
Do not separate L2/3, L3/4, L4/5 by middle or posterior height (means within 0.4-1.2 mm, SDs 1.0-1.9 mm); use anterior height and wedge with vertebral measures.
Condition disc heights on sex: men 5-31 percent taller anteriorly depending on level; posterior heights at L3/4-L5/S1 and all L5/S1 measures do not differ by sex.

Do not treat a narrow disc as age-normal: the three-point average changes little with age in healthy people (Inference: narrowing suggests degeneration); expect FH to fall with age (women every level, men L2/3 down).
Do not use adult norms below 20 years: teenagers' three-point averages are smaller than the 20s at every level (Inference).
These are recumbent CT values; position may change them and MRI may differ (Inference: standing films may read lower).
In a possibly transitional spine, decide which disc is the last mobile one before applying the L5/S1 row; the paper gives no rule (Inference).

Measure FH on each side as the greatest distance between cranial pedicle lower border and caudal pedicle upper border; average sides; expect a peak at L2/3 (19.5/18.6 mm) and a minimum at L5/S1 (14.3/14.4 mm).
Build the bone surface at a bone threshold (226-3071 HU) and cut each vertebra free of neighbours' articular processes and T12 of its rib before placing points.

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none; no prevalence of LSTV, L6, T13 or rib variants and no handling rule (p. e107, PDF 2).

(b) Panjabi's papers have no disc or foraminal heights (Inference, panjabi1991c note). This paper adds junction emissions between consecutive instances: anterior, middle, posterior midsagittal disc heights and left-right FH, T12/L1 to L5/S1, by sex (Table 6, p. e113, PDF 8; Table 6 Average = AP average); adult or age-specific priors from Tables 2-5 weighted by Table 1. Inference: neighbouring disc heights are likely correlated within a spine; independent draws add jitter.

(b) Mask biases (Inference): 226 HU surface vs SPINEPS boundary up to about one voxel per disc height; straight vs perpendicular distance unstated (matters at wedged L5/S1); middle height depends on endplate concavity, a minimum gap reads lower; marginal osteophytes shorten rim heights; FH needs a pedicle subregion (S1 pedicle at L5/S1).
(b) No cervical or thoracic discs: nothing for C3-T11 junctions. The L5/S1 row assumes a five-lumbar spine; the decoder's numbering decides which disc it describes.

(c) Measurement error: none reported. Inference: assume about one CT slice spacing per height until a reliability study gives a figure; Table 6 SDs (0.8-2.9 mm disc, 1.5-2.1 mm FH) are between-subject spread.

(d) Sex: strong T12/L1-L3/4 (anterior ratio 1.31-1.19, middle 1.09-1.15, posterior 1.06-1.15, FH 1.03-1.06), none at L5/S1 (1.00-1.05) (Inference from Table 6). Age small (Tables 7-8): men middle rises at T12/L1-L2/3, rims fall only at L4/5, FH falls L2/3-L5/S1; women anterior falls L3/4-L5/S1, posterior L1/2-L4/5, FH every level. Pooled values include 16 teenagers.

(d) Body size: no relation of disc height to stature, weight or BMI reported (attempted, incomplete data; p. e114, PDF 9); stature probably in inches (Inference). Population: one US centre, ethnicity not reported, supine abdominal CT of patients with non-spinal complaints.
gaps: Table 6's Average disc height row equals (anterior+posterior)/2, not the three-point mean defined in the text and given in the abstract and Figure 8 (Inference from arithmetic).

Conclusions give the L4/5 maximum as 8.9 +/- 1.7 (men) and 8.6 +/- 1.8 (women); results give L4/5 9.2/8.5, and 8.6 is women's L5/S1; men's 8.9 matches Figure 8's L5/S1 8.90 (Inference: L5/S1 values printed as L4/5); in women L5/S1 (8.57) exceeds L4/5 (8.46).

Largest height 9.87 +/- 0.7 mm in men's eighth decade: no table or Table 1 group covers 80+, yet Figures 2-7 plot an 80 point; figures' 10 point differs from the tables' first decade (L4/5 men 9.16 vs 8.73); captions promise two series but plot one per sex (Inference: figures drawn from data including subjects 80+).
Ages: methods 10-80, abstract 14-83/14-89, results 14-79; men's mean 48 vs 47; stature subset includes a man of 80.
Text says women smaller at P < 0.001 at all levels except L5/S1, but posterior heights at L3/4 (0.079) and L4/5 (0.705) do not differ and some P are 0.001 or 0.005.
Text calls women's FH correlations moderate to strong (|R| 0.241-0.447) and women's L4/5 posterior moderate (R -0.248).
Table 8's first column is headed Average Disc Height (twice); the text shows it is anterior height.
Table 12 men's age-weight R printed -1.67 (impossible; Inference -0.167, recomputed about -0.165).
Table 4 men's L1/2 left FH fifth decade SD truncated (17.91 +/- 1.).

Decade-table slips (Inference): men T12/L1 first decade Average 4.72/AP 4.26 vs 4.81/4.41; men L3/4 first decade 7.62/6.67 vs 7.90/7.04; men L4/5 first decade AP 8.7 vs 8.07; men L5/S1 sixth decade AP 8.71 vs 8.14; women L1/2 seventh decade Average 5.81 vs 5.59; FH Average men T12/L1 third decade 16.43 vs 16.34, women L4/5 first decade 17.63 vs 17.45.
Tables 9-10: printed BMI disagrees with weight and height by > 1 kg/m2 in at least five rows each (Inference).
Elliptization partly contradicted by own tables: women's posterior heights fall at L1/2 and L2/3; men's L3/4 shows no change.
Sex called a strong correlation but only t-tests given; paired left-right FH test never reported.

Not reported: scanner, slice thickness, voxel size, number excluded, ethnicity, level counting, transitional anatomy, reliability, distance convention, disc angle, endplate dimensions, body heights, lordosis, disc height vs stature.

Inference (other papers): radiograph and MRI series usually put the tallest mid-disc at L4/5 with L5/S1 lower in the middle, as here; anterior L5/S1 tallest fits lordosis; the 10 mm cage limit applies to the three-point average, not anterior height used for lateral or anterior cages.
